top_news.title: HMI Medical Unveils New Brand Identities Across Its Healthcare Facilities in Malaysia As Regional Cross-border Healthcare Grows
top_news.summary: The refreshed identities of HMI Medical's hospitals and medical centre in Malaysia signal the Group's commitment to deliver more with care by sparking change for the future of healthcare SINGAPORE and KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HMI Medical is strengthening its regional healthcare network by introducing refreshed brand identities for its tertiary hospitals in Johor and Melaka. Featuring the HMI Spark and the Group's signature green and blue brand colours, the refreshed identities strengthen the hospitals' connection to HMI Medical while building on more than three decades of healthcare heritage and the trust they have established with patients and partners. This alignment strengthens the Group's brand recognition among patients and partners, providing a stronger foundation for the hospitals' expansion plans and HMI Medical's continued regional growth. Sparking change across four priorities to shape the future of healthcare The HMI Spark represents HMI Medical's ambition to deliver More with Care by bringing together four essential elements of total care: physical, mental, social and personalised. These reflect the Group's commitment to caring for people's physical health, understanding their mental and emotional needs, personalising care to each individual, and connecting with the communities in which they live. Formed by four converging "more-than" chevrons, the Spark symbolises HMI Medical's ambition to deliver healthcare differently by continuously innovating to create better ways to care for every patient. This ambition is brought to life through four priorities: More expertise: Strengthening clinical capabilities, specialist knowledge and medical technology to deliver high-quality, personalised care. More ways to care: Expanding services, specialties and care settings to address a wider range of healthcare needs, from prevention to treatment and recovery. More connected experiences: Connecting expertise, services and care settings to create a more coordinated healthcare journey that is easier for patients to navigate. More trusted care within reach: Making quality healthcare more accessible and affordable, giving individuals and families greater confidence in their care choices. Ms. Chin Wei Jia, Group CEO of HMI Medical, said the refreshed identities reflect the Group's response to growing cross-border healthcare demand, driven by population growth and stronger connectivity between Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia. She added, "the HMI Spark represents our commitment to driving meaningful change in healthcare and creating better experiences for patients. Bringing our hospitals and healthcare facilities under a shared identity makes it easier for patients to recognise that wherever they receive care from HMI Medical, they are part of one trusted network, united by the same commitment to quality and care. It also reflects our ambition to work as one Group to spark positive change for the future of healthcare. Delivering more with care across the region Alongside the refreshed logo, Mahkota Medical Centre will be renamed toMahkota Specialist Hospital (MSH). The new name emphasizes its evolution over more than three decades, with deep specialist and subspecialist capabilities, multidisciplinary care and advanced medical technology. It also reinforces Mahkota's positioning as a comprehensive tertiary hospital serving patients from Melaka and across the region. With a new hospital block under development, MSH is set to become the largest private hospital in Melaka by 2029, with a total capacity of up to 430 beds. Established in 2009, Regency Specialist Hospital (RSH) will continue to grow its clinical capabilities and position itself for its next phase of growth to be the largest private hospital with a total capacity of up to 500 beds in Southern Malaysia with its newly completed expansion building equipped with a comprehensive cancer centre, next-generation smart wards and enhanced specialist services. Launched in 2024, Regency Medical Care Centre(RMCC) will also retain its existing name as it continues to enhance its capabilities to become a convenient one-stop healthcare hub with outpatient care services to patients around the region. Planned additions include day surgery, endoscopy and other outpatient services will be launched to provide a highly connected patient journey between the hospital and the medical centre. HMI Medical will also be expanding into East Malaysia with Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching, a 300-bed capacity SMART tertiary hospital, expected to open in 2029. As HMI Medical expands its healthcare facilities, clinical services and technological capabilities, its people remain at the heart of healthcare. The Group is investing RM50 million over five years through the HMI Malaysia Healthcare Workforce 2030 Fund to support scholarships, education sponsorships and clinical attachments, equipping healthcare professionals with the skills and experience to deliver quality care and meet the needs of patients in Malaysia and across the region. Shaping the next frontier of cross-border care The expansions of Mahkota Specialist Hospital (MSH), Regency Specialist Hospital (RSH) and Regency Medical Care Centre (RMCC) and the development of Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching (RSHK) reflect HMI Medical's long-term investment in clinical capabilities, patient experience and access to specialist and tertiary care, supporting Malaysia's ambition to become a leading regional healthcare hub. In 2024, Malaysia welcomed more than 1.6 million healthcare travellers, generating approximately RM2.7 billion in revenue.[1] Reflecting HMI Medical's longstanding role in serving cross-border healthcare needs, its hospitals in Johor and Melaka have been approved for overseas MediSave use since 2010. They remain the only private hospitals in their respective states with this approval, enabling eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to use their MediSave savings for approved hospitalisations and day surgeries, subject to prevailing requirements.[2] Mr. Stanley Lam, Country CEO of HMI Malaysia, said cross-border healthcare is reshaping Malaysia's role as a regional healthcare hub. "By investing in clinical capabilities, infrastructure, technology and healthcare talent, we aim to strengthen care for local communities we serve while meeting the growing regional demand. Mahkota and Regency have built strong reputations in their respective markets, including among international patients. With a stronger shared identity and continued investment in our capabilities, we are well positioned to build on these foundations and extend our reach across the region." As healthcare needs evolve and patients increasingly look beyond national borders for care, the Group will continue to build on its regional experience to help shape the future of healthcare in the region where quality care is more accessible, connected and personalised to the communities it serves. END About HMI Medical Founded and headquartered in Singapore, HMI Medical is a leading regional healthcare group with over three decades of healthcare delivery across Southeast Asia. The Group operates an integrated healthcare ecosystem across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam, spanning managed care, primary care, specialist care, diagnostics, ambulatory care, tertiary hospitals and healthcare training. HMI Medical supports more than 4 million lives annually, with over 400 doctors and 3,000 employees. The Group is committed to making quality healthcare more accessible through connected, patient-centred care across the region. For more information, please visit www.hmimedical.com About the logo (The HMI Spark) At the heart of HMI Medical's brand identity is the HMI Spark, formed by four converging "more-than" chevrons that symbolise the Group's ambition to go beyond conventional healthcare. The Spark brings together four essential elements of total care - physical, mental, social and personalised - reflecting HMI Medical's commitment to caring for the whole person. It also represents the Group's promise of More with Care, expressed through four priorities: More expertise, More ways to care, More connected experiences and More trusted care within reach. The blue chevron reflects the trust built over the years, evolving into an integrated healthcare platform that connects services and expertise in Singapore and Malaysia. The green chevron connects HMI Medical to its rich healthcare heritage while representing its commitment to a sustainable future of healthcare. top_news.title: Black Panther Party stalwarts to celebrate 1966 founding in Oakland, programs that aided the poor - myMotherLode.com
top_news.summary: The legacy of the Black Panther Party lives on six decades after its founding, in the work of a Seattle medical center started to address systemic health disparities in the African American community. Originally known as the Sidney Miller Free Medical Clinic, it was part of the local Black Panther Party chapter's plan to uplift Black residents, an effort mirrored in survival programs across the country. As the celebration begins Thursday for the Black Panther Party’s Oct. 15, 1966, founding, former members are looking beyond the black leather jackets, berets and clenched fists to programs aimed at healing disenfranchised and forgotten communities.

articles.title: HMI Medical Unveils New Brand Identities Across Its Healthcare Facilities in Malaysia As Regional Cross-border Healthcare Grows
articles.summary: The refreshed identities of HMI Medical's hospitals and medical centre in Malaysia signal the Group's commitment to deliver more with care by sparking change for the future of healthcare SINGAPORE and KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HMI Medical is strengthening its regional healthcare network by introducing refreshed brand identities for its tertiary hospitals in Johor and Melaka. Featuring the HMI Spark and the Group's signature green and blue brand colours, the refreshed identities strengthen the hospitals' connection to HMI Medical while building on more than three decades of healthcare heritage and the trust they have established with patients and partners. This alignment strengthens the Group's brand recognition among patients and partners, providing a stronger foundation for the hospitals' expansion plans and HMI Medical's continued regional growth. Sparking change across four priorities to shape the future of healthcare The HMI Spark represents HMI Medical's ambition to deliver More with Care by bringing together four essential elements of total care: physical, mental, social and personalised. These reflect the Group's commitment to caring for people's physical health, understanding their mental and emotional needs, personalising care to each individual, and connecting with the communities in which they live. Formed by four converging "more-than" chevrons, the Spark symbolises HMI Medical's ambition to deliver healthcare differently by continuously innovating to create better ways to care for every patient. This ambition is brought to life through four priorities: More expertise: Strengthening clinical capabilities, specialist knowledge and medical technology to deliver high-quality, personalised care. More ways to care: Expanding services, specialties and care settings to address a wider range of healthcare needs, from prevention to treatment and recovery. More connected experiences: Connecting expertise, services and care settings to create a more coordinated healthcare journey that is easier for patients to navigate. More trusted care within reach: Making quality healthcare more accessible and affordable, giving individuals and families greater confidence in their care choices. Ms. Chin Wei Jia, Group CEO of HMI Medical, said the refreshed identities reflect the Group's response to growing cross-border healthcare demand, driven by population growth and stronger connectivity between Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia. She added, "the HMI Spark represents our commitment to driving meaningful change in healthcare and creating better experiences for patients. Bringing our hospitals and healthcare facilities under a shared identity makes it easier for patients to recognise that wherever they receive care from HMI Medical, they are part of one trusted network, united by the same commitment to quality and care. It also reflects our ambition to work as one Group to spark positive change for the future of healthcare. Delivering more with care across the region Alongside the refreshed logo, Mahkota Medical Centre will be renamed toMahkota Specialist Hospital (MSH). The new name emphasizes its evolution over more than three decades, with deep specialist and subspecialist capabilities, multidisciplinary care and advanced medical technology. It also reinforces Mahkota's positioning as a comprehensive tertiary hospital serving patients from Melaka and across the region. With a new hospital block under development, MSH is set to become the largest private hospital in Melaka by 2029, with a total capacity of up to 430 beds. Established in 2009, Regency Specialist Hospital (RSH) will continue to grow its clinical capabilities and position itself for its next phase of growth to be the largest private hospital with a total capacity of up to 500 beds in Southern Malaysia with its newly completed expansion building equipped with a comprehensive cancer centre, next-generation smart wards and enhanced specialist services. Launched in 2024, Regency Medical Care Centre(RMCC) will also retain its existing name as it continues to enhance its capabilities to become a convenient one-stop healthcare hub with outpatient care services to patients around the region. Planned additions include day surgery, endoscopy and other outpatient services will be launched to provide a highly connected patient journey between the hospital and the medical centre. HMI Medical will also be expanding into East Malaysia with Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching, a 300-bed capacity SMART tertiary hospital, expected to open in 2029. As HMI Medical expands its healthcare facilities, clinical services and technological capabilities, its people remain at the heart of healthcare. The Group is investing RM50 million over five years through the HMI Malaysia Healthcare Workforce 2030 Fund to support scholarships, education sponsorships and clinical attachments, equipping healthcare professionals with the skills and experience to deliver quality care and meet the needs of patients in Malaysia and across the region. Shaping the next frontier of cross-border care The expansions of Mahkota Specialist Hospital (MSH), Regency Specialist Hospital (RSH) and Regency Medical Care Centre (RMCC) and the development of Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching (RSHK) reflect HMI Medical's long-term investment in clinical capabilities, patient experience and access to specialist and tertiary care, supporting Malaysia's ambition to become a leading regional healthcare hub. In 2024, Malaysia welcomed more than 1.6 million healthcare travellers, generating approximately RM2.7 billion in revenue.[1] Reflecting HMI Medical's longstanding role in serving cross-border healthcare needs, its hospitals in Johor and Melaka have been approved for overseas MediSave use since 2010. They remain the only private hospitals in their respective states with this approval, enabling eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to use their MediSave savings for approved hospitalisations and day surgeries, subject to prevailing requirements.[2] Mr. Stanley Lam, Country CEO of HMI Malaysia, said cross-border healthcare is reshaping Malaysia's role as a regional healthcare hub. "By investing in clinical capabilities, infrastructure, technology and healthcare talent, we aim to strengthen care for local communities we serve while meeting the growing regional demand. Mahkota and Regency have built strong reputations in their respective markets, including among international patients. With a stronger shared identity and continued investment in our capabilities, we are well positioned to build on these foundations and extend our reach across the region." As healthcare needs evolve and patients increasingly look beyond national borders for care, the Group will continue to build on its regional experience to help shape the future of healthcare in the region where quality care is more accessible, connected and personalised to the communities it serves. END About HMI Medical Founded and headquartered in Singapore, HMI Medical is a leading regional healthcare group with over three decades of healthcare delivery across Southeast Asia. The Group operates an integrated healthcare ecosystem across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam, spanning managed care, primary care, specialist care, diagnostics, ambulatory care, tertiary hospitals and healthcare training. HMI Medical supports more than 4 million lives annually, with over 400 doctors and 3,000 employees. The Group is committed to making quality healthcare more accessible through connected, patient-centred care across the region. For more information, please visit www.hmimedical.com About the logo (The HMI Spark) At the heart of HMI Medical's brand identity is the HMI Spark, formed by four converging "more-than" chevrons that symbolise the Group's ambition to go beyond conventional healthcare. The Spark brings together four essential elements of total care - physical, mental, social and personalised - reflecting HMI Medical's commitment to caring for the whole person. It also represents the Group's promise of More with Care, expressed through four priorities: More expertise, More ways to care, More connected experiences and More trusted care within reach. The blue chevron reflects the trust built over the years, evolving into an integrated healthcare platform that connects services and expertise in Singapore and Malaysia. The green chevron connects HMI Medical to its rich healthcare heritage while representing its commitment to a sustainable future of healthcare. articles.title: Black Panther Party stalwarts to celebrate 1966 founding in Oakland, programs that aided the poor - myMotherLode.com
articles.summary: The legacy of the Black Panther Party lives on six decades after its founding, in the work of a Seattle medical center started to address systemic health disparities in the African American community. Originally known as the Sidney Miller Free Medical Clinic, it was part of the local Black Panther Party chapter's plan to uplift Black residents, an effort mirrored in survival programs across the country. As the celebration begins Thursday for the Black Panther Party’s Oct. 15, 1966, founding, former members are looking beyond the black leather jackets, berets and clenched fists to programs aimed at healing disenfranchised and forgotten communities.
